newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Memphis, Hong Kong busiest cargo airports in Nov - ACI.
newsitem.headline: Memphis, Hong Kong busiest cargo airports in Nov - ACI.

text.p: World airports led by Memphis and Hong Kong saw steady growth in cargo traffic in November 1996 but the increase in passenger traffic was slow, the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) said on Monday.

Memphis, base of U.S. express freight carrier Federal Express, was the world's busiest cargo airport in November 1996 with 167,015 tonnes, up 16.9 percent over a year ago, followed by Hong Kong with 159,300 tonnes, up 14.9 percent.
The ACI said cargo traffic handled by 473 airports around the world grew 9.7 percent to 4.4 million tonnes in November over a year ago.
North America, the biggest of ACI's six cargo-handling regions, reported 2.26 million tonnes of cargo traffic, up 7.5 percent over November 1995.

Airports in the Asia/Pacific region (in which ACI incorporates Indo-China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia and Australia), had 942,400 tonnes of cargo traffic, an increase of 11.7 percent.

November cargo traffic handled at ACI's Europe member airports totalled 935,800 tonnes, up 7.4 percent and that at Middle East airports was 139,850 tonnes, up 16.9 percent. Latin America/Caribbean airports had 114,800 tonnes, up 37.5 percent.
African airports recorded the highest growth rate of ACI's cargo-handling regions in November with a 103.6 percent increase to 43,500 tonnes.
The ACI said passenger traffic grew 3.5 percent to 189.3 million travellers in November.

Europe airports had the largest passenger growth with 8.7 percent to 52.9 million travellers in November, followed by African airports with 6.8 percent to 2.05 million. Passenger traffic in North America fell 0.2 percent to 92.7 million.

The ACI said Chicago's O'Hare airport held its position as the world's busiest passenger airport with 5.2 million travellers in November, 1.3 percent up over a year ago, followed by Atlanta with 4.9 million, up one percent. - Reuters Geneva Newsroom 41-22-733 38 31
